_REGENERATION_IS_GATED_BYTE_IDENTICAL: tests/test_arc_magnitude_migrated.py::test_mg5_the_seed_regenerates_byte_identically re-runs this builder and diffs. VALUE_N is LIFTED from seeds/arc_goals.json at build time, so if ag_select ever changes this seed goes out of date LOUDLY instead of silently ranking by a value term that no longer matches the one it claims to be a reading of.
_SELF_LOAD_ONLY_RATIONALE: substrate/boot_all.py::_read_seeds GLOBS seeds/*.json and installs every match at boot, so a file here is live in EVERY agent in the tree the moment it lands. seeds/arc_goals.json ships self_load_only for that reason and this seed DEPENDS ON IT, so shipping this one globbed would activate a chain whose base is deliberately gated. REMOVING THIS KEY IS THE TREE-WIDE ACTIVATION and needs the paired sweep A5 requires.
description: CONSTRAINTS, ORDER-N PROJECTED VALUE, AND THE MAGNITUDE LADDER (MG1-MG3). seeds/arc_goals.json ranks arc goals by ABSOLUTE HEADROOM IN TASKS -- a SPOT valuation, priced in a vacuum. Three terms were missing and A9 registers all three as missing INPUTS rather than hazards needing guards. (1) CONSTRAINTS: horizon, scope and competing requirements land as ArcConstraint nodes with holds_under -> ResidualCondition, so gr_condition_lapse / gr_condition_hold lapse and restore them VERBATIM -- zero new lapse machinery -- and the ask requests them under T2 IGNORANCE. (2) ORDER-N VALUE: a goal carrying a MEASURED TIER LADDER is worth the horizon-truncated sum of its per-order increments, each discounted by attrition factors READ FROM RESULTS ARTIFACTS at named dotted paths -- there is NO attrition number in this file. A projection with no measured basis carries a fact_equals(arc_measure_epoch) condition and EXPIRES at the next epoch. (3) THE LADDER: small absorb / medium balance / huge push back, routed by RATIOS against the measured horizon with no authored cutoff anywhere. v1.1.0 (A16/MG4): mg_goal_order_n_default gains ONE additive exclusion (a goal carrying parent_agid -- a decomposition child, seeds/arc_decompose.json) so the generic order-N fallback cannot silently overwrite a child's own discounted orderN_headroom_n back to its undiscounted headroom_n. INERT ON EVERY EXISTING SCENE: no goal on the shipped graph carries parent_agid. Decomposition ITSELF (mg_decompose, the child mint, the terminal status) lives in the SEPARATE seeds/arc_decompose.json, not here -- this seed still only sets decompose_required and names the measured ladder a split would use.

microtheory.name: arc_goal_magnitude
microtheory.description: A goal is not expensive in the abstract -- it is correct at twelve months and wrong at two weeks. A horizon is a conditioned fact that lapses like any other measurement; a projection beyond order 1 is a claim that must name the artifact it rests on or expire; and how big something is is a RATIO against a measured budget, never a number someone chose.

attrs.name: default_arc_magnitude_policy
attrs._w_out_of_scope_is_AUTHORED: AUTHORED policy on a node, tunable as graph data without touching a rule -- the RESIDUAL_SCALE=100 / w_unsignatured precedent. It is a WEIGHT, not a veto: an out-of-scope goal stays in the pool and can still win on merit, which is the whole point of A9's framing correction. Gated two-position (it can flip the outcome in both directions); no principled value.
attrs._THE_RUNG_THRESHOLDS_ARE_NOT_HERE: DELIBERATELY. MG3 registers that thresholds are RATIOS against the MEASURED horizon and never authored constants, because an authored cutoff is gameable exactly the way cost_bits is. The only number in mg_rung is 1.0, and 1.0 is not a tuning knob -- it is what 'fits' MEANS once cost and horizon are in the same measured unit (operator units, from arc6_structural_ceiling.json::bundles.n_units). There is no small_ratio and no huge_ratio to tune.

attrs.name: horizon
attrs.description: the budget, in the SAME MEASURED UNIT the tier ladder's cost is denominated in (operator units). A goal is not 'too expensive' in the abstract -- it is correct at twelve months and wrong at two weeks, and without this term every goal is priced in a vacuum.

attrs.name: scope
attrs.description: which seams are in scope. An out-of-scope goal is CHARGED w_out_of_scope and stays in the pool -- a weight, not a filter.

attrs.name: competing
attrs.description: a competing requirement CONSUMES the horizon (HORIZON_NET = gross - sum of competing), so it reprices every goal through the channel that already exists rather than adding a second knob.

attrs.name: inventory_to_strict_reach
attrs._why: DISCOUNT ONE OF THE TWO THE ARTIFACT ITSELF NAMES. arc6_structural_ceiling.json::inventory_ceiling_is_not_reach says in its own words: 'the honest expected CONVERSION for a bundle is its inventory count discounted twice -- once by size/reach, once by the S4 pass-rate prior'. This is the first: of the 10 ids B0's inventory covers, only those with a WITNESS INSIDE THE ENUMERATOR'S OWN BUDGET are reachable at all.
attrs._NO_NUMBER_IS_STORED_HERE: numerator_n / denominator_n / resolved are written by domains/arc_magnitude_ingest.resolve_attrition_keys from the artifact at the paths above, and `factor` is computed by mg_attrition_factor as Div(numerator_n, denominator_n). If the path does not walk, `resolved` is 0.0 and the factor is NULL -- which every consumer coalesces to 0.0, so an unmeasured projection is worth NOTHING rather than its undiscounted increment.

attrs.name: reach_to_conversion
attrs._why: DISCOUNT TWO. arc-4 S4 moved 25 tasks off `gapped:enumerate_failed` and only 8 were fully correct -- the same corpus, the same enumerator, the same protocol. THIS IS THE PER-ORDER FACTOR: reaching order k+1 requires order k to have CONVERTED first, so it compounds once per order. It is also the number the prereg's own HS1 bar was derived from (10 x 0.32 = ~3.2 expected), which returned 0 -- see the calibration record.
attrs._NO_NUMBER_IS_STORED_HERE: numerator_n / denominator_n / resolved are written by domains/arc_magnitude_ingest.resolve_attrition_keys from the artifact at the paths above, and `factor` is computed by mg_attrition_factor as Div(numerator_n, denominator_n). If the path does not walk, `resolved` is 0.0 and the factor is NULL -- which every consumer coalesces to 0.0, so an unmeasured projection is worth NOTHING rather than its undiscounted increment.

attrs.name: seam_a_honest_vs_cherry_picked
attrs._why: READ AND REPORTED, DELIBERATELY NOT USED AS AN ORDER FACTOR. Seam A's 5/8/14/27/60 is a GRANULARITY ladder, not an UNLOCK ladder: it inflates by renaming the same move at finer grain, and the prereg's own standing rule says 'in an import seam audit the NAMING; in a structural seam audit the PRICE'. Feeding a naming ladder into an order sum would be counting the same tasks four times. Recorded here so that declining to use it is visible rather than silent.
attrs._NO_NUMBER_IS_STORED_HERE: numerator_n / denominator_n / resolved are written by domains/arc_magnitude_ingest.resolve_attrition_keys from the artifact at the paths above, and `factor` is computed by mg_attrition_factor as Div(numerator_n, denominator_n). If the path does not walk, `resolved` is 0.0 and the factor is NULL -- which every consumer coalesces to 0.0, so an unmeasured projection is worth NOTHING rather than its undiscounted increment.

rules.name: mg_attrition_factor
rules.comment: MG2. THE FACTOR IS COMPUTED, NOT STORED. The adapter writes only numerator_n and denominator_n -- the literal contents of a named artifact at a named dotted path -- and this rule divides them. There is no attrition number anywhere in seeds/arc_magnitude.json, which is the strongest available form of A9's 'READ not authored': not a number with a citation next to it, but no number at all. Guarded on `resolved`, so an artifact whose path did not walk leaves `factor` ABSENT rather than 0.0 -- and absent is what the expiry lane keys on, because 'we could not measure it' and 'we measured zero' must not collapse into the same fact.

rules.name: mg_tier_survival
rules.comment: MG2. Stamps each measured tier with its survival factor so the order sum can read it, and so the discount is AUDITABLE PER TIER rather than buried inside one expression. Re-armed whenever the factors change (guarded on the stamped survival differing from the computed one would churn; guarded on ABSENCE plus a resolved factor is the terminating form).

rules.name: mg_tier_in_horizon
rules.comment: MG1/MG3. THE HORIZON TRUNCATES THE ORDER SUM. A tier whose CUMULATIVE cost exceeds the net horizon is not buyable, so it contributes nothing -- which is how ONE horizon answer reprices the whole pool instead of returning the single bit an approve/deny gate would. Cumulative, not marginal, because the ladder's tiers are NESTED (B1 CONTAINS B0's eight units); charging the marginal cost would price a tier as if the ones below it were free. MEASURED HAZARD, and it is why NO_HORIZON is checked FIRST: Gt(8.0, null) is TRUE on this engine, so a graph that had never been told a horizon would have read as one on an impossible deadline and truncated every tier to nothing.

rules.name: mg_projection_mint_measured
rules.comment: MG2. A PROJECTION IS A CLAIM AND THEREFORE CARRIES A CONDITION. A goal with a measured tier ladder gets ONE ArcProjection whose holds_under condition is fact_equals(arc6_structural_ceiling_present == '1') -- so it lapses through gr_condition_lapse THE MOMENT ITS EVIDENCE ARTIFACT CHANGES, and not before. Same node type, same edge, same rule as the six measured ceilings: ZERO NEW LAPSE MACHINERY, which is MG1's registered constraint applied to MG2's projection. The mirror (mg_projection_mint_unmeasured) is this rule's guard with ATTRITION_MEASURED negated, so exactly one of the pair fires.

effects._why: both attrition factors resolved from artifact paths, so this projection has a measured basis and survives until that artifact changes.

effects.why: the attrition factors are quoted from this artifact; if it changes the projection must be re-read, not re-used.

rules.name: mg_projection_mint_unmeasured
rules.comment: MG2's REGISTERED BAR, MADE MECHANICAL: *a projection with no measured basis must default-expire at the next epoch, exactly as an unconditioned human answer does.* Its condition is fact_equals(arc_measure_epoch == <epoch at mint>) -- the SAME default ag_reply_mints_testimony_unconditioned uses, on the same ResidualFact, consumed by the same gr_condition_lapse branch. Angluin's zero-bits result made mechanical, applied to the agent's OWN projections rather than to a human's answer: a projection that cannot name what it rests on is worth one epoch. This is the lane that keeps an authored projection from being 'unbounded in the dangerous direction' -- it does not forbid one, it makes it decay.

effects._why: an attrition path did not walk, so this projection rests on nothing measured and expires at the next measurement epoch.

effects.why: no measured basis, so it expires at the next measurement epoch -- an unconditioned projection is worth one epoch.

rules.name: mg_goal_order_n
rules.comment: MG2, THE HEADLINE. A goal with a MEASURED TIER LADDER is valued at the horizon-truncated sum of its per-order increments, each discounted by its own measured survival -- not at its top tier's paper inventory. On the shipped graph this is the difference between 42 (B3's inventory, i.e. every task the ladder would ever cover, credited in full and at once) and ~13.6 (B0's 10 measured directly, plus 16/6/10 discounted by the attrition the artifacts record). The order-1 reading was ALREADY a projection -- it just had no attrition on it, which is exactly the unbounded direction A9 names. REQUIRES A NON-STALE PROJECTION: once the projection lapses, mg_goal_order_n_default takes over and the goal falls back to its order-1 headroom, which is what 'default-expire' MEANS here.

rules.name: mg_goal_order_n_default
rules.comment:
A9, VERBATIM: *'Re-measurement's order-1 value IS its total value (completing it unlocks nothing).'* A goal with no measured ladder -- or whose projection has EXPIRED -- has no orders above 1, so its order-N headroom IS its order-1 headroom. This is not a fallback for missing data; it is the correct answer for a goal that unlocks nothing, and it is why order-N reprices SOME goals and not others rather than rescaling all of them uniformly. Guard is mg_goal_order_n's with the ladder/projection items negated, so exactly one of the pair fires.
A16/MG4 ADDITION, ADDITIVE AND INERT ON EVERY EXISTING SCENE: this rule is ALSO excluded for a decomposition CHILD (parent_agid set). Without the exclusion, this rule would unconditionally recompute ANY laddered-orphan goal's orderN_headroom_n FROM ITS RAW headroom_n every fixpoint pass -- a decomposition child has no proposed_seam (deliberately, MG4 6.2(1)), so _has_ladder(child) is False and this rule's ORIGINAL guard alone would match it, silently overwriting mg_child_order_n's discounted headroom_n*tier_survival back to the undiscounted headroom_n -- precisely the order-1-credit inflation trap MG4 6.2(4) names. No goal on the shipped graph carries parent_agid, so this exclusion is False (inert) on every scene MG1-3/5 already measured.

rules.name: mg_rung
rules.comment:
MG3. THE LADDER ROUTES BY RATIO AND THERE IS NO AUTHORED CUTOFF. r = cost_total / horizon_net, r_first = cost_of_the_smallest_measured_increment / horizon_net, both in OPERATOR UNITS -- the unit arc6_structural_ceiling.json::bundles.n_units is denominated in, which is why the two sides of the ratio are commensurable without a conversion anyone chose.
  r <= 1                    ABSORB     the whole goal fits; execute, do not ask
  r > 1 and r_first <= 1    BALANCE    part of it fits; compete in the collapse
  r_first > 1               PUSH_BACK  not even the smallest measured
                                       increment fits -> ask for scope AND decompose
THE ONLY NUMBER HERE IS 1.0, AND 1.0 IS NOT A KNOB -- it is what 'fits' means once both sides are in the same measured unit. There is no small_ratio and no huge_ratio to tune, which is the difference between this and cost_bits. NO_HORIZON is a FOURTH outcome and is checked first, both because Gt(x, null) is TRUE on this engine and because 'we have not been told' is a real state that must not masquerade as 'it fits' -- it is precisely the state mg_ask_constraints exists to leave.

rules.name: mg_scope_charge
rules.comment: MG1. Scope lands as a CHARGE, never as a filter. If any non-stale scope constraint is held and this goal's sig_seam is not among them, it is charged w_out_of_scope inside VALUE_N -- it stays in the pool and can still win. A9's framing correction is the whole reason: three guards were proposed and all three were a missing input dressed as a hazard. Scope is a missing INPUT, so it is a TERM. Note the guard reads sig_seam and NOT proposed_seam: an unsignatured goal is illegible to scope exactly as it is illegible to every residual, and it already pays w_unsignatured for that in the lifted order-1 term.

rules.name: mg_scope_clear
rules.comment: THE OTHER DIRECTION, AND IT IS REQUIRED. gr_condition_lapse is deliberately not latched, so a scope constraint CAN come back and CAN go away; a one-way charge would be a second un-lapsable claim -- the exact defect gr_condition_hold exists to prevent. Clears to 0.0 EXPLICITLY rather than unsetting, because this engine has no unset_attr and a null would sort BELOW any number in any later comparison (measured: Lt(null, 0.0) is TRUE). AND IT STAMPS THE 0.0 ON A NEVER-CHARGED GOAL TOO, guarding on Not(Eq(_, 0.0)) rather than on Eq(_, 1.0): 'in scope' and 'never looked at' would otherwise be the same absent attr, and this tree has already lost a deferred claim to exactly that conflation. Terminates -- once 0.0 is stamped the guard is false.

rules.name: mg_select
rules.comment: MG2/MG3, THE ORDER-N COLLAPSE. ag_select's twin over THE SAME POOL, machine-lifted from seeds/arc_goals.json, ranking by the SAME VALUE TERM with exactly one Attr key swapped (headroom_n -> orderN_headroom_n) and the scope charge subtracted. That is what makes 'order-N differs from order-1 on the shipped graph' a MEASUREMENT rather than a comparison of two things someone wrote separately: the same instrument reads the same nodes twice, and the only thing that changed is the term under test. A7's rule -- a control must be shown capable of detecting the difference it is used to rule out -- is satisfied structurally here, because the two readings are the same expression. Stamps mg_* alongside ag_select's arc_sel_*, so BOTH orderings are readable off one graph at one time and neither has to be re-derived.

rules.name: mg_select_audit
rules.comment: The audit stamp, binding the winner by its OWN stamped agid rather than re-deriving it -- ag_select_audit's shape and its reason: if this rule and mg_select ever disagreed about who won, the audit would be describing a different ranking from the one that fired.

rules.name: mg_select_runner_up
rules.comment: THE ORDER-N MARGIN. Split out for ag_select_runner_up's two measured reasons: deriving the winner inside the runner-up's own pool predicate embeds the whole lifted VALUE subtree once per use AND evaluates it once per pool element (that took arc_goals' seed to 2.4 MB), and this engine has NO RULE ORDERING, so the dependency mg_select -> mg_select_runner_up has to be a GUARD CHAIN keyed on the previous rule's stamp.

rules.name: mg_select_margin
rules.comment: The order-N margin itself, with the runner-up bound by its stamped agid. Reported next to ag_select's own arc_sel_margin so the repricing is readable as a NUMBER, not just as a reordering: on the shipped graph the two collapses disagree about the WINNER, and the margin is what says by how much.

rules.name: mg_ask_constraints
rules.comment:
MG1. THE ASK IS FOR THE CONSTRAINT, NOT FOR APPROVAL, AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT. A per-goal approval returns ONE BIT about ONE goal; ONE horizon answer reprices EVERY goal that has a ladder, because the horizon truncates the order sum. That asymmetry is the reason to ask constraints rather than permissions, and it is measured in results/arc6_magnitude.json rather than argued.
TRIGGER IS T2 IGNORANCE, matching AG-4's discrimination: fire when NO horizon constraint currently holds. The distinction that matters is ignorance vs refutation -- a horizon that is held and CURRENT means the graph has been told and is not ignorant, so it does not ask; a horizon that has LAPSED means its reason is gone and asking again is correct, which falls out of _live_constraints reading `stale` rather than mere existence. RATE BOUND: one open question per measurement epoch, re-entry gated on NEW MEASUREMENT and never on graph churn (the codebook_epoch form).
EVERY NUMBER IN THE TEXT GOES THROUGH ToJsonString: StringConcat SILENTLY DROPS numeric parts, which would have produced a question that looked fine and said nothing.

parts.value: arc goals and I hold NO horizon, so I am pricing every one of them in a vacuum. My largest candidate carries a MEASURED tier ladder costing
operator units end to end, with its smallest buyable increment at

. I am not asking you to approve a goal -- that would return one bit about one goal. WHAT IS THE HORIZON, in those same units? One answer reprices all of them, because a horizon truncates how far down a ladder I can buy. Name a checkable condition with it, so the answer can lapse when its reason does; without one it expires at my next measurement epoch.

rules.name: mg_constraint_from_reply_conditioned
rules.comment: MG1's CORE: A CONSTRAINT IS A CONDITIONED FACT, THROUGH THE EXISTING MACHINERY. The reply mints an ArcConstraint with a holds_under edge to a ResidualCondition -- and gr_condition_lapse / gr_condition_hold match on the holds_under EDGE with NO TYPE RESTRICTION on their left var, so they lapse and restore an ArcConstraint verbatim. ZERO NEW LAPSE MECHANISM, which is exactly what MG1 registers. Verified live before this seed was written: an ArcConstraint with a fact_equals condition goes stale when the fact mismatches and comes back when it matches again. This branch is the one where the reply NAMED A CHECKABLE REASON, so the horizon survives until that reason is falsified -- a deadline that cannot lapse is a lie with a long half-life, and a horizon is the most load-bearing claim in the whole collapse.

effects._never_parsed: the ckind and the numbers come from the con_* attrs the world adapter wrote, never from the reply text. A string-derived constraint is Seam C at arc grain.

effects.why: named by the reply -- a reason that can be falsified

rules.name: mg_constraint_from_reply_unconditioned
rules.comment: THE DEFAULT CONDITION, AND IT IS THE POINT. A constraint answer naming no checkable reason gets fact_equals(arc_measure_epoch == <epoch at reply>), so IT EXPIRES AT THE NEXT MEASUREMENT EPOCH and the pool reverts to being priced in a vacuum -- visibly, through mg_rung's 'unknown_no_horizon', rather than silently continuing to use a stale deadline. Guard is the conditioned rule's with the cond_kind item NEGATED, so exactly one of the pair fires.

effects._never_parsed: the ckind and the numbers come from the con_* attrs the world adapter wrote, never from the reply text. A string-derived constraint is Seam C at arc grain.

effects.why: the reply named no checkable reason, so this constraint expires at the next measurement epoch.
